newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida, union sign two-year wage contract.
newsitem.headline: Escondida, union sign two-year wage contract.

text.p: Minera Escondida Ltda and its 350-member union signed a two-year collective wage contract Friday, clearing the way for the union to lift a strike in effect since April 18, union president Hugo Fernandez.
Striking workers at the mine, the world's largest copper pit, are returning to the job in accordance with their shift schedule, Fernandez said.
The head of the company's negotiating committee, Ricardo Serrano, signing the contract for Escondida, said Fernandez. There was no comment at company headquarters in Santiago.
The strikers, about 15 percent of Escondida's work force, decided to lift the walkout after some expressed an interest in returning to work, said Fernandez.

Under Chilean law, if more than 50 percent of the workers return to work voluntarily after two weeks on strike, the walkout automatically loses its legal status and an employer is free to fire the strikers. But before any firings, unions usually agree to lift the strike.

But Escondida officials said on Wednesday that the two-week provision would take on Saturday -- not Friday. The lifting of the strike before the two-week mark suggested the union leadership saw support for the walkout weakening.

"We were coming up to day 15, and since some workers were indicating that they wanted to return to work, the membership opted to accept the company's last wage offer," said Fernandez. The contract they signed was essentially the same one offered by Escondida before the strike, he said.
Officials at the mine, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary, have consistently denied the strike had any effect on production, though they admitted it was slowing down operations.

The mine's non-unionized majority will now have the option of joining the union contract if they want to. Non-unionized workers have individual contracts with the company, so it will be up to each one of them to decide whether to go for the union contract, Escondida officials have said.
